item.description:
Things done

Both of these packages have no maintainers, and are using EOL Electron 41. Waveterm's bundled Electron is quite old as well, and has a CVE filed against it. These packages have had months to have been updated. We have marked Electron 41 as vulnerable in Nixpkgs now, so this is matching what we do in-tree. Drop them on unstable since there are no maintainers to ping, so I don't expect anything to happen soon.

Marked them as vulnerable for backport cherry-picking.

item.title: iwd: add patchset to fix exploitable memory-safety bugs
item.description:
47 days ago, this blog post was published containing PoCs exploiting several memory safety bugs in IWD. Mostly these just were able to cause the daemon to crash, but notably on ARM32 they were able to get full remote code execution. Since there is no semantic compiler guarantee preventing remote code execution, any compiler version bump may introduce an RCE even on a nixpkgs-supported platform.

The reporter claimed to have disclosed this to the IWD maintainers in May, but there has been zero activity on the IWD repo since March of this year. I reached out to the IWD maintainers, and James Prestwood (a former Intel employee and frequent IWD contributor) got back to me saying:

I'm working with Marcel/Denis to get maintainer rights. Denis isn't going to be able to get to reviews any time soon. I've been reviewing as I have time, but don't have rights on the repo to push anything.

Alongside the PoCs, the reporter also published patches to IWD which he claims fix the memory safety issues. I asked James about these, and he confirmed:

I've reviewed [the patches from the blog post] and afaict they look fine and shouldn't cause any regressions.

So it looks like IWD is effectively unmaintained (in that everybody with commit access to their repo is MIA), but these patches are approved by the closest thing to an active maintainer. Since IWD is still in widespread use, I think that the responsible thing to do is add these patches to protect our users. In the alternative, we should mark IWD as insecure.

Things done

I've added the patches provided by the reporter and approved by James Prestwood to IWD.
